title: Enterprise Prospect Playbook: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Deck, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook is a single-reference sales enablement artifact for enterprise prospects evaluating Redwood Inference. It consolidates positioning and messaging, short competitive briefs and battlecards, a recommended pitch-deck outline, practical pricing guidance for discovery calls, two representative case studies, and a prospect-facing Security FAQ. Intended audience: AE/SE teams, solutions engineers, and marketing content owners.

Key value proposition (one-liner):
Redwood Inference provides production-grade LLM serving that makes inference predictable, cost-effective, and secure across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — so engineering teams can ship LLM features without building custom serving infrastructure.

Positioning pillars (use in discovery and pitch):
- Production-first performance and reliability: SLAs, latency SLOs, autoscaling and predictable throughput for mission-critical apps.
- Cost-aware controls: batching, caching, and quantization recommendations tied to unit economics.
- Unified deployment model: same API + tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private environments.
- Enterprise-grade security & compliance: VPC/private control plane options, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logging, and SOC/ISO/GDPR alignment.

Messaging guidance (opening statements):
- For Product/Engineering: “Redwood reduces the time and risk of deploying LLM features by providing a single runtime that scales, optimizes cost, and preserves model quality.”
- For Platform/SRE: “Redwood abstracts hardware and capacity management with observability, rollout controls, and predictable performance under load.”
- For Security/Legal: “Redwood supports private deployments, granular audit logs, and customer-managed keys to meet regulatory and data-residency requirements.”

Competitive brief (90-second summary):
- OpenAI-hosted APIs: Strong model quality & developer ecosystem; weaker when enterprises need private deployments or predictable reserved GPU capacity. Positioning: emphasize Redwood’s dedicated/private options, and cost controls tied to SLOs.
- Cloud vendor endpoints (Google/AWS/Microsoft): Enterprise-grade controls and global regions; often higher cost for token-heavy workloads and inconsistent latency for bursty inference patterns. Positioning: call out Redwood’s cost-aware runtime optimizations and compact deployment options.
- Self-hosted runtimes / inference vendors: Offer deeper control but require substantial engineering to reach production SLOs. Positioning: emphasize Redwood’s product with built-in observability, rollout controls, and managed upgrades.

Competitive battlecard (one-liners + rebuttals):
- "We’ll just host models ourselves": Rebuttal — Building and operating a production inference stack (batching, KV cache, kernel selection, safety regressions) costs months of engineering and ongoing ops. Redwood delivers these features with measurable cost/latency gains and migration support.
- "We already use cloud vendor endpoints": Rebuttal — For sustained, token-heavy workloads, Redwood’s Dedicated and Optimize features typically reduce unit cost and improve tail latency. Offer to run a simple cost/latency pilot using customer traces.
- "OpenAI has better models": Rebuttal — Redwood supports a curated catalog of high-quality open and licensed models and can route requests to higher-capacity variants or fall back to hosted models as part of an SLA-backed policy.

Pitch deck recommended outline (10–12 slides):
1) Title & ask — One-line value prop and desired next step (pilot / technical workshop).
2) Customer context — What we know about the prospect’s use cases and current pain points.
3) Redwood at a glance — Product modes (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) and differences.
4) Architecture & orchestration — High-level diagram showing request routing, caching, batching, and fallbacks.
5) Performance & economics — Representative latency/throughput benchmarks and unit-cost drivers.
6) Reliability & operations — SLOs, tracing, rollout controls, and observability screenshots.
7) Security & compliance — VPC options, KMS integrations, SOC/ISO evidence summary, and data residency.
8) Pricing & commercial fit — Example pricing scenarios (see pricing guidance below).
9) Case studies & outcomes — 2–3 brief customer wins with metrics.
10) Pilot plan & success criteria — 30/60/90-day technical pilot with milestones.
11) Technical appendix — Model catalog, integration steps, API examples.
12) Call to action & contacts — AE/SE/solutions engineering points of contact.

Pricing guidance (discovery-level scripts + examples):
- Pricing pillars to surface in discovery: monthly token volume, peak RPS, latency SLOs, data residency needs, need for reserved capacity vs. pay-as-you-go, and SLA/response-time contractual requirements.
- Common commercial configurations and discovery prompts: 
  1) Hosted (self-serve): Pay-as-you-go per 1K tokens + optional premium support. Best for rapid prototyping and lower-volume product features.
  2) Dedicated (reserved capacity): Monthly/annual committed GPU pools with predictable throughput + burst capacity and an SLA. Best for sustained, production workloads.
  3) Private (VPC/on-prem): Platform license + integration and support fees; used by regulated customers requiring a private control plane or air-gapped deployment.

Example pricing scenarios (discovery examples you can quote qualitatively on a call):
| Scenario | Indicative model | Commercial fit | Key levers |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Prototype chatbot | Hosted API | Low volume, fast time-to-value | Pay-as-you-go tokens, single model |
| Customer support at scale | Dedicated | High sustained tokens, strict latency | Reserved capacity, autoscaling policy |
| Regulated financial services | Private | Data residency & audit requirements | Private control plane, KMS, extended support |

NOTE: Use commercialization team for formal quotes. Always collect logs/trace examples during discovery to run a pilot-based estimate.

Pilot playbook (30/60/90 day):
1) Discovery (Week 0–1): capture sample traces, peak profiles, and success metrics (cost/latency/accuracy).
2) Technical kickoff (Week 2): solutions engineer runs integration checklist: API keys, model selection, prompts, and eval harness.
3) Pilot run (Week 3–6): run production-like traffic (or replay traces), collect metrics for latency, cost per 1K tokens, and quality regressions.
4) Review (Week 7): present pilot results with action items; recommend Dedicated sizing or Private deployment if warranted.
5) Rollout plan (Week 8–12): staged rollout, canary rules, and rollback criteria.

Representative case studies (two short vignettes):
1) Customer: Fintech payments platform — Challenge: slow and inconsistent invoice extraction at scale.
   Solution: Migrated NLU inference to Redwood Dedicated with KV caching and batching; added prefix cache for recurring templates.
   Outcome: 3x throughput increase, 45% reduction in per-inference cost, and 98.7% reduction in tail latency incidents over 90 days.

2) Customer: B2B SaaS knowledge assistant — Challenge: regulatory requirement for EU data residency and audit trails.
   Solution: Deployed Redwood Private (VPC) in EU region with customer-managed KMS and audit logging.
   Outcome: Passed customer compliance review, reduced audit prep time by 60%, and achieved SLA-backed latency targets.

Security FAQ for prospects (concise answers for sales and SEs):
Q: Where is customer data stored and how long is it retained?
A: Data residency depends on deployment mode: Hosted allows region selection with configurable retention windows; Dedicated and Private give customers control over storage location and retention policies. We retain logs per contract; default retention for non-prod logs is 30 days unless extended.

Q: Do you offer customer-managed encryption keys (CMKs)?
A: Yes. For Dedicated and Private deployments, Redwood supports KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys for encryption-at-rest. Hosted customers can enable CMKs for workspace-level keys where supported.

Q: Can we run Redwood fully on-prem / air-gapped?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports on-prem packaging for regulated customers. Our engagement model includes an onprem packaging plan, deployment runbook, and transfer of operational runbooks to the customer SRE team.

Q: What compliance attestations do you provide?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence and provides artifacts to customers under NDA. For regulated customers we supplement with architecture reviews, penetration testing reports, and contractual commitments.

Q: How do you handle model governance and data leakage concerns?
A: We provide model version pinning, restricted model catalogs, and audit trails that map request IDs to models and runtime variants. For sensitive workloads we recommend Private deployment and model filtering policies.

Q: What observability is available during pilot and production?
A: Per-request latency traces, token-level cost breakdowns, per-model dashboards, error rates, and alerting hooks. Solutions engineers will configure dashboards during pilots.

Operational and ownership notes:
- Primary AE owner: populate the pilot success criteria and maintain the engagement timeline.
- Primary SE owner: run the technical checklist and maintain the pilot dashboard.
- Legal/Procurement: involve early for Private engagements (licensing and support addenda).
